To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the most important parameters to consider when designing a programme to acquire hydrochemical data from deep boreholes are the timing and location of sampling, the method of fluid extraction, the method of sample collection, the method of analysis and the method of flushing used during drilling.

the most important design considerations for the acquisition of hydrochemical data from deep boreholes are: (1) to use a cutting method that minimises contamination of the borehole wall; (2) to use a flushing method that minimises the amount of drilling fluid that is left in the borehole; (3) to use a fluid extraction testing tool that minimises the disturbance of the borehole fluid column; (4) to use a bottomhole assembly that minimises the potential for cross-contamination

the most important parameters that affect the quality and/or quantity of hydrochemical information that is obtained from deep boreholes are: the type of drilling fluid used (water based is preferable); the method of flushing the borehole after drilling (water based is preferred); the method of extracting fluids from boreholes (pumped is preferred); the timing of sampling relative to fluid extraction testing (as early as possible is preferred); the number of samples collected (as many as possible is preferred), and the analytical method used

, for any given site, there are a number of key design parameters that should be considered during the development of a final design for the acquisition of hydrochemical data from deep boreholes.
